findings.summary: New read-only guard covers formula cells but not spill ghosts / pivot cells, so `toggleCheckboxAt` still reports `true` for a write that silently never happens
findings.evidence: The guard added at sheet.ts:3842 is `if (cell?.f) return false;`. A spill ghost cell (array-formula output, `cell.spillAnchor` set, no `f`) passes the guard, so `toggleCheckboxValue` + `await this.setData(ref, next)` runs — but `setData` bails at sheet.ts:1004 (`if (existing?.spillAnchor) return;`) and, for a pivot sheet, at sheet.ts:995 (`if (this.pivotDefinition) return;`). No write occurs, yet `toggleCheckboxAt` returns `true`. Callers treat `true` as "state changed": packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:365 re-renders on it and packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4853 renders only when true, so the return value is now wrong for exactly the same class of read-only cell the guard was added for. Correct behavior for a formula-driven (spilled) checkbox is the same no-op-and-return-false as `cell.f`.

findings.summary: Formula-guard test comment claims "writes no literal" but never asserts that no `v` was written
findings.evidence: The new test says `// Toggle is a no-op: reports false, keeps the formula, writes no literal.` and then only asserts `toggleCheckboxAt(...) === false` and `cell?.f === '=1=1'`. It never asserts anything about `cell?.v`, so a regression that wrote a literal `TRUE` alongside/over the formula's computed value (or that wrote to a different ref, e.g. a non-anchor merged ref) would still pass. An `expect(cell?.v)` assertion against the formula result (or `toEqual` on the whole cell) would close the gap the comment claims to cover.

findings.summary: Case-fold gate keys on `=== undefined`, so an empty-string custom value silently disables the new default-boolean case folding (and makes the rule un-checkable)
findings.evidence: `if (rule.checkedValue === undefined && rule.uncheckedValue === undefined)` at data-validation.ts:163 treats `checkedValue: ''` (or `uncheckedValue: ''`) as "custom", falling through to `value === checkedValueOf(rule)` where `checkedValueOf` uses `??` (line 140) and therefore returns `''` — no non-empty value can ever be checked, and `toggleCheckboxValue` writes `''` (which `setData`/`isEmptyCell` turns into a cell delete). `normalizeDataValidationRule` (lines 66-101) does not strip or defaultize empty checkbox values, so a rule persisted with `''` from an import or API reaches this path. Pre-existing for the exact-match branch, but the new gate now also loses the case-insensitive behavior for such a rule.

findings.summary: No test covers a rule with only a custom `checkedValue` (uncheckedValue undefined) — one half of the new two-part guard is unverified
findings.evidence: The new guard is `rule.checkedValue === undefined && rule.uncheckedValue === undefined`. The three new tests cover (a) both undefined (line 93), (b) both set (line 107), (c) only `uncheckedValue` set (line 118). No test sets `checkedValue: 'Yes'` while leaving `uncheckedValue` undefined. Consequently the mutation of dropping the `checkedValue === undefined` conjunct (leaving only `rule.uncheckedValue === undefined`) passes the entire suite: the both-undefined case still case-folds, the both-set case still takes the exact-match branch, and the uncheckedValue-only case still takes the exact branch. findings.summary: New `value.toUpperCase()` on document-supplied cell value can throw on a non-string `v` in the per-repaint render path
findings.evidence: Before this change `isCheckboxChecked` only did `value === checkedValueOf(rule)`, which is total for any runtime type. The new fallback at data-validation.ts:166 calls a String method on `value`, which comes straight from `cell?.v` in the render loop (packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1042). `Cell.v` is typed `string | undefined` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/types.ts:187) but that is a compile-time guarantee only: cell records are hydrated from the collaborative Yorkie document, and the normalizer at packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:215-216 forwards `cell.v` unvalidated (`if (cell.v !== undefined && cell.v !== '') normalized.v = cell.v`). Attack chain: a co-editor (the backend grants read+write to everyone with document access — see packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:178, no viewer role) writes a numeric/`null` `v` into a cell covered by a default checkbox rule; every other client's canvas repaint then hits `value.toUpperCase()` → TypeError inside `renderCellCheckbox`, breaking rendering of the shared document for all viewers (persistent client-side DoS, since the bad value stays in the CRDT). I could not confirm a concrete producer of a non-string `v` inside the repo (the xlsx importer sets `parsed.v` from XML text, i.e. a string, and `readonly.ts:33 toCell()` coerces), and the same file already calls `value?.trim()` in `isValidListValue` (line 202), so the pattern is pre-existing — hence low confidence and hardening-level severity. A `typeof value !== 'string'` early return (or `String(value)`) makes the new branch total.

findings.summary: Formula read-only guard lives only in the model helper; write authorization for checkbox toggles remains view-layer-only (no bypass found)
findings.evidence: I enumerated every caller of the toggle path to check the new guard cannot be reached unguarded: `Sheet.toggleCheckboxAt` (sheet.ts:3834) is called from `Spreadsheet.toggleCheckboxAt` (view/spreadsheet.ts:363-368, gated on `this._readOnly`), the click path (view/worksheet.ts:3385-3405, gated on `!this.readOnly`) and the Space-key path (view/worksheet.ts:4844-4856, gated on `!this.readOnly`); no other caller exists in packages/. `toggleCheckboxValue`/`isCheckboxChecked` are additionally re-exported from packages/sheets/src/index.ts:89-90,267-268, so an embedder can compute a value and call `setData` directly, bypassing the new `cell?.f` guard — but that is an ordinary write, and the model layer has no `readOnly` concept at all (`grep readOnly packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts` → no matches), so the guard is an integrity/UX rule rather than a security control. Recording this as a no-bypass result, not a defect the diff introduced.

findings.summary: New formula read-only guard covers `cell.f` only; spill *ghost* cells (formula-driven, `spillAnchor` set, no `f`) still fall through and `toggleCheckboxAt` returns `true` for them although `setData` silently drops the write
findings.evidence: The guard added at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3842 tests `cell?.f`. A dynamic-array ghost cell is written by calculator.ts:128 as `{ v, spillAnchor: sref }` — it has no `f`, so a checkbox over a spill range passes the new guard, reaches `setData` at sheet.ts:3846, which bails at sheet.ts:1004 (`if (existing?.spillAnchor) return;`). No value is written, yet `toggleCheckboxAt` still returns `true`, so packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:366 repaints and reports a toggle that never happened (and the Space handler at worksheet.ts:4853 renders on a no-op). The same 'formula drives the state' invariant the diff enforces for `f` should also cover `cell.spillAnchor`; the fix belongs on the new guard.

findings.summary: `value.toUpperCase()` is now called on a value that was only ever compared with `===` before — any non-string `Cell.v` reaching the render path throws instead of rendering unchecked
findings.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/data-validation.ts:166 dereferences `value`. The per-repaint caller packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1042 passes `cell?.v` straight from the store grid. `Cell.v` is typed `string | undefined` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/types.ts:187), so tsc protects in-repo callers, but `isCheckboxChecked` is a public export (packages/sheets/src/index.ts:89/267) and store contents can originate from JSON/Yorkie/xlsx/REST paths where a `null` or numeric `v` is not type-checked. +# Checkbox data-validation bug fixes
+
+Follow-ups from the data-validation design doc (`docs/design/sheets/data-validation.md`,
+Phase-1 "Not yet guarded" note). Two clear correctness bugs in the shipped
+checkbox control, each self-contained.
+
+## Bugs
+
+1. **Formula cell is not read-only under a checkbox rule.**
+   `Sheet.toggleCheckboxAt` (`sheet.ts:3834`) reads `cell?.v` and writes a
+   literal `TRUE`/`FALSE` via `setData` without checking `cell.f`. Toggling a
+   checkbox that sits over a formula cell **overwrites the formula**. Design
+   intent: a formula-backed checkbox is read-only (the formula drives the
+   state) — Google Sheets / Excel parity. Both the click path
+   (`worksheet.ts:3405`) and the Space path (`worksheet.ts:4853`) route through
+   `toggleCheckboxAt`, so one guard fixes both.
+
+2. **`isCheckboxChecked` is case-sensitive.**
+   `isCheckboxChecked` (`data-validation.ts:149`) compares `value === 'TRUE'`
+   exactly, so a cell holding `"true"` renders **unchecked**. `setData`
+   normalizes typed input to `"TRUE"`, but values arriving via xlsx import /
+   REST API / external paste can be lowercase and bypass normalization. The
+   formula engine (`formula.ts:1054`) and input parser (`input.ts:242`) already
+   treat `TRUE`/`FALSE` case-insensitively; the render/toggle path should match.
+   Fix scope: **default boolean checkbox only** (no custom `checkedValue`) —
+   a custom checked value stays an exact string match (GS parity).
+
+## Plan (TDD)
+
+- [x] Model test: `isCheckboxChecked` matches `"true"`/`"True"`/`"TRUE"` for a
+      default rule; a custom-value rule stays exact-match.
+- [x] Model fix: `isCheckboxChecked` case-insensitive for the fully-default
+      boolean checkbox only; `toggleCheckboxValue` inherits the fix (delegates).
+- [x] Sheet test: `toggleCheckboxAt` over a formula cell is a no-op — returns
+      `false`, leaves `cell.f` intact, writes no `v`.
+- [x] Sheet fix: guard `toggleCheckboxAt` on `cell?.f`.
+- [x] `pnpm test` (sheets) green; `pnpm verify:fast` green (EXIT 0).
+- [x] Update design doc Phase-1 "Not yet guarded" note (both now fixed).
+
+## Review
+
+High-effort workflow code review (`Workflow code-review`, 4 finders + verify)
+surfaced two findings, both addressed:
+
+- **[0] correctness (PLAUSIBLE)** — case-fold branch was gated only on
+  `checkedValue === undefined`, so a rule with a custom `uncheckedValue` that
+  upper-cases to `"TRUE"` inverted state. Fixed: case-folding now requires
+  *both* custom values absent; added a regression test.
+- **[1] cleanup (CONFIRMED)** — `value.toUpperCase()` allocated per repaint,
+  against the file's no-alloc convention. Fixed: canonical `TRUE`/`FALSE`
+  short-circuit before the `toUpperCase` fallback.
+
+A refuted finding ("silently depends on `CHECKBOX_TRUE` being uppercase") was
+dismissed by the verifier — `CHECKBOX_TRUE` is a module constant.
+
+Both bugs are model/Sheet-level; the click and Space view paths route through
+`toggleCheckboxAt` and the render path through `isCheckboxChecked`, so no
+view-layer change was needed. View-layer smoke deferred (Phase-1 precedent).
+
+## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)
+
+- Space range-uniform "set all checked" (parity feature, not a bug).
+- Merged-cell glyph/hit-test mismatch.
+- Eager `FALSE` materialization for `COUNTIF`.
+- Custom checkbox values UI.
+
+## Review
+

samples.summary: New `value.toUpperCase()` on document-supplied cell value can throw on a non-string `v` in the per-repaint render path
samples.evidence: Before this change `isCheckboxChecked` only did `value === checkedValueOf(rule)`, which is total for any runtime type. The new fallback at data-validation.ts:166 calls a String method on `value`, which comes straight from `cell?.v` in the render loop (packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1042). `Cell.v` is typed `string | undefined` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/types.ts:187) but that is a compile-time guarantee only: cell records are hydrated from the collaborative Yorkie document, and the normalizer at packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:215-216 forwards `cell.v` unvalidated (`if (cell.v !== undefined && cell.v !== '') normalized.v = cell.v`). Attack chain: a co-editor (the backend grants read+write to everyone with document access — see packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:178, no viewer role) writes a numeric/`null` `v` into a cell covered by a default checkbox rule; every other client's canvas repaint then hits `value.toUpperCase()` → TypeError inside `renderCellCheckbox`, breaking rendering of the shared document for all viewers (persistent client-side DoS, since the bad value stays in the CRDT). I could not confirm a concrete producer of a non-string `v` inside the repo (the xlsx importer sets `parsed.v` from XML text, i.e. a string, and `readonly.ts:33 toCell()` coerces), and the same file already calls `value?.trim()` in `isValidListValue` (line 202), so the pattern is pre-existing — hence low confidence and hardening-level severity. A `typeof value !== 'string'` early return (or `String(value)`) makes the new branch total.

samples.summary: Formula read-only guard lives only in the model helper; write authorization for checkbox toggles remains view-layer-only (no bypass found)
samples.evidence: I enumerated every caller of the toggle path to check the new guard cannot be reached unguarded: `Sheet.toggleCheckboxAt` (sheet.ts:3834) is called from `Spreadsheet.toggleCheckboxAt` (view/spreadsheet.ts:363-368, gated on `this._readOnly`), the click path (view/worksheet.ts:3385-3405, gated on `!this.readOnly`) and the Space-key path (view/worksheet.ts:4844-4856, gated on `!this.readOnly`); no other caller exists in packages/. `toggleCheckboxValue`/`isCheckboxChecked` are additionally re-exported from packages/sheets/src/index.ts:89-90,267-268, so an embedder can compute a value and call `setData` directly, bypassing the new `cell?.f` guard — but that is an ordinary write, and the model layer has no `readOnly` concept at all (`grep readOnly packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts` → no matches), so the guard is an integrity/UX rule rather than a security control. Recording this as a no-bypass result, not a defect the diff introduced.

samples.summary: New formula read-only guard covers `cell.f` only; spill *ghost* cells (formula-driven, `spillAnchor` set, no `f`) still fall through and `toggleCheckboxAt` returns `true` for them although `setData` silently drops the write
samples.evidence: The guard added at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3842 tests `cell?.f`. A dynamic-array ghost cell is written by calculator.ts:128 as `{ v, spillAnchor: sref }` — it has no `f`, so a checkbox over a spill range passes the new guard, reaches `setData` at sheet.ts:3846, which bails at sheet.ts:1004 (`if (existing?.spillAnchor) return;`). No value is written, yet `toggleCheckboxAt` still returns `true`, so packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:366 repaints and reports a toggle that never happened (and the Space handler at worksheet.ts:4853 renders on a no-op). The same 'formula drives the state' invariant the diff enforces for `f` should also cover `cell.spillAnchor`; the fix belongs on the new guard.

samples.summary: `value.toUpperCase()` is now called on a value that was only ever compared with `===` before — any non-string `Cell.v` reaching the render path throws instead of rendering unchecked
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/data-validation.ts:166 dereferences `value`. The per-repaint caller packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1042 passes `cell?.v` straight from the store grid. `Cell.v` is typed `string | undefined` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/types.ts:187), so tsc protects in-repo callers, but `isCheckboxChecked` is a public export (packages/sheets/src/index.ts:89/267) and store contents can originate from JSON/Yorkie/xlsx/REST paths where a `null` or numeric `v` is not type-checked. Previously such a value merely compared unequal; now it throws a TypeError inside the canvas repaint loop. To confirm, one would need a store/import path that can persist a non-string `v`.

verdict.reason: Every element of the presence claim checks out. data-validation.ts:166 does call `value.toUpperCase()` unguarded, reached whenever the value is neither canonical 'TRUE' (164) nor 'FALSE' (165). gridcanvas.ts:1042 calls it per repaint with `cell?.v`; sheet.ts:3845 reaches the same code via toggleCheckboxValue (data-validation.ts:178). types.ts:187 declares `v?: string`, so only tsc protects in-repo callers, and index.ts:89/267 export the function publicly. I then looked for the store path the reviewer said was needed to confirm, and found one: packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts:111 types the request body inline (no DTO class), and :122 writes `v: body.value ?? existing?.v ?? ''` directly into the Yorkie doc, with the batch endpoint doing the same at :155/:170; the global ValidationPipe (backend/src/main.ts:60-61) skips inline `Object` metatypes, so a numeric/null `value` is persisted unchecked and syncs to the client render loop. Candidate refutations fail: the xlsx importer only yields strings (xlsx-importer.ts:200-207), and the pre-existing unguarded dereferences (data-validation.ts:202 via gridcanvas.ts:1151, sheet.ts:4078) do not execute for a checkbox-ruled cell because isValidValueForRule short-circuits to `true` for checkbox (data-validation.ts:315) — so nothing already crashes or guards this path. In-lane for blast radius (behaviour change to an exported symbol with untyped external consumers) and blocking: a TypeError inside the canvas repaint loop.
